rows.note: This is the all-purpose noun for the act of running or going jogging.

example.english: I went for a run this morning for half an hour.
example.traditional: 我朝早跑步跑咗半個鐘。
example.jyutping: ngo5 ziu1 zou2 paau2 bou6 paau2 zo2 bun3 go3 zung1

rows.note: This is the all-purpose choice for physically running, including running a distance or competing in a race.

example.english: I run in the park every morning.
example.jyutping: ngo5 ziu1 zou2 heoi3 gung1 jyun4 paau2 bou6

rows.note: Use this when a liquid flows or comes out of something, as in a river flowing or a nose running.

example.english: My nose is starting to run.
example.jyutping: ngo5 go3 bei6 hoi1 ci2 lau4 bei6 seoi2

rows.note: Use this for one quick errand or one scheduled journey, rather than the route itself.

example.english: I’m going to run to the convenience store now.
example.jyutping: ngo5 ji4 gaa1 heoi3 jat1 zyun2 bin6 lei6 dim3

rows.note: Use this for going or hurrying away, especially fleeing from trouble rather than literally running on foot.

example.english: When the alarm went off, everyone had to run away.
example.jyutping: ging2 bou3 jat1 hoeng2 daai6 gaa1 zau6 jiu3 zau2

rows.note: Use this for the route itself, including a transport route or a route taken while running.

example.english: This bus run will change next month.
example.traditional: 呢條巴士路線下個月會改。
example.jyutping: ni1 tiu4 baa1 si2 lou6 sin3 haa6 go3 jyut6 wui5 goi2

rows.note: Use this in sports for a sustained scoring surge by one team, not for an ordinary running play or general streak.

example.english: We finally held off their scoring run after a sustained attack.
example.traditional: 對手一輪攻勢之後，我哋終於頂住咗。
example.jyutping: deoi3 sau2 jat1 leon4 gung1 sai3 zi1 hau6 ngo5 dei6 zung1 jyu1 ding2 zyu6 zo2

rows.note: Use this when someone manages or is in charge of a shop, business, or other responsibility.

example.english: I run the family shop now.
example.traditional: 我而家幫屋企人打理間舖。
example.jyutping: ngo5 ji4 gaa1 bong1 uk1 kei2 jan4 daa2 lei5 gaan1 pou3
